newsitem.title: USA: Conn Gov opposes plan to tax Indian casinos--paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn Gov opposes plan to tax Indian casinos--paper.

text.p: Connecticut Gov John Rowland and Congressional Democrat leaders plan to fight a proposal to tax Native American gaming, which could cut how much the state gets from casinos, the Hartford Courant said Wednesday.

Under a tax plan proposed by U.S. Representative Bill Archer, R-Texas, a 35 percent tax would be imposed on casinos and other tribal business activities, as part of his $85 billion, five-year tax reduction plan.

The proposal would limit a tribe's tax deduction while adding to its costs. At least a part of the $200 million annual payment that the Mashantucket Pequots and the Mohegans make to the state's coffers could be in jeopardy, the governor said, according to the paper.

Precisely how Archer's proposal would work was not yet clear. The paper quoted the governor as saying "I don't know what the proposed tax is from the federal side, and whether that would affect the gross revenue from the slot machines. There could be some arguments made either way. But indeed, if you're taking more out of the pie, something else will give."

There was speculation that the tribes' options could include a reduction in the slot revenue payments to the state, or a decision that with the addition of the federal tax burden, the tribes would no longer make the payments to the state to preserve their slot machine monopoly, the paper said.
